change: For multi-member Matter working reads, settle fresh READ_WORK_ITEM grants first, then load tenant-scoped WorkItem projections and exact source identity in one SQL statement for that request group. A single member keeps its original reader.
invariants: Every linked and saved WorkItem receives a fresh object access decision on each request; denied groups execute no projection batch.
Selected WorkItem rows are tenant-scoped, and the four required source registration joins remain subject to PostgreSQL RLS.
The granted documentVersionId is compared against the selected WorkItem, and projection/source document and version identities are checked before returning a binding.
Projection parsing precedes source validation and follows request order. Historical saved members remain in groups of four, and both Matter version confirmations remain.
No source or permission result is cached across requests; no schema, role, tenant policy, or formal adoption path changed.

isolatedPostgres.comparisonMethod: Same fixed local fixture; candidate and exact parent implementations run separately against the same isolated database and existing full Matter test. Raw logs remain in local temporary storage.

explicitCases: batch waits for all fresh grants
each required source table hidden by RLS fails
malformed projection and missing source retain error precedence

limits: Local query counts and millisecond timings do not establish published latency or p95.
Published 1df traces showed no overlap of SQL spans, but that observation does not prove a general driver property.
A multi-member current composition uses one batch for all current linked WorkItems; saved historical members retain groups of four.
Independent review, selective integration, release, and same-sample deployed timing/background competition remain pending.
